blocks.x: Language is now an engineering surface. Applied AI & Generative AI runs seven practices that turn models into governed production systems — retrieval that cites its sources, tuning that never regresses silently, vision that feeds systems of record, and one platform that keeps every model call observable, bounded and affordable.

The domain covers the full surface where language and prediction models carry enterprise work: strategy that survives procurement, platform engineering that holds under audit, retrieval that cites, tuning that does not regress, and vision and conversational systems wired into the tools staff already use.

Seven practices run under one evaluation discipline. A model change, a corpus change or a prompt change is the same event class — versioned, graded, and gated — because in production they are all just changes to the answer.

blocks.x: What separates a production program from a stalled pilot

Language models are commodity infrastructure now; what separates a working program from a stalled one is everything around the model — the corpus, the permissions, the evaluation, the cost line and the surface where staff actually meet the answer.

This domain runs those seven practices as one system. Strategy picks the fights worth having, the platform makes every model call observable and bounded, retrieval and tuning make answers defensible, and vision and conversation put the work inside operational tools rather than another tab nobody opens.

The disciplines are shared across practices: one eval harness, one model registry, one guardrail stack, one cost model. That is what lets a team move from pilot to production without re-earning trust for every new use case.

blocks.caption: Domain-level release gates — the evidence each demands
rows: Is there a signed metric with an owner?
Baseline document signed by the metric owner; collection method attached
Is the knowledge estate ready to be retrieved?
Source inventory with freshness SLAs, dedup and permission scan results
Does the system beat the bar on the eval suite?
Suite version pinned; groundedness, citation precision and regression count at or above target
Does it refuse what it should refuse?
Red-team suite results; jailbreak and prompt-injection containment evidence
Cost per 1k calls at target load with caching on, plus a burn-down plan if over
Would this survive a regulator's afternoon?
Trace samples with citations, permission decisions and prompt versions attached
